docs.task: How the repo brief lists the workspace's books and caps the list.

asks: Explain how the repo brief lists the workspace's books
Explain how the brief caps that list

data_flow.step: The factory builds a spawn for an agent and reads the workspace's books from disk.
BooksBrief::read calls book::list(workspace) and returns None when it is empty, so no books section appears. Otherwise it stores dir and the whole list.

book::list reads every directory in `<workspace runtime>/docs` whose name passes is_book_id, parses each book.json, maps it to a BookSummary, and sorts by updated_at descending then id ascending. It applies no limit.
When the agent's definition has Capability::DocsSearch, the factory sets search_tool to the executor-specific tool name from tool_name("docs_search", agent, executor).
The factory passes books: books.as_ref() in BriefInput to augment, which skips the brief when the first message already carries a heading, else calls build_brief and appends the result after `---`.

build_brief renders the books section: takes the first MAX_BRIEF_BOOKS (20) books, which are the newest 20 because the list is sorted newest first. Each line is `- `<dir>/<id>/index.md`: <projects> (<n> sections[, with the system architecture])`. If more than 20 exist it adds `- and N more; find them with Glob in <dir>`. Then the intro sentence says to search with the tool name (Rule B8) or to read the sections that bear on the task.

docs.task: How workspace settings reach the spawn factory and the brief, and how a setting is validated at save.

asks: How workspace settings reach the spawn factory
How workspace settings reach the brief
How a setting is validated at save

data_flow.step: The browser or API client sends the whole WorkspaceSettings as JSON. `POST /api/workspaces/{id}/validate` returns the issues and writes nothing. `PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}` saves.

patch_workspace calls WorkspaceRt::save_settings and maps an Err(issues) through ApiErr::invalid to a 422 body `{error, issues}`. On success it renames the registry workspace when `name` changed and returns WorkspaceDetail.

save_settings calls WorkspaceRt::validate. validate calls validate_settings with the global config, the machine Environment, and the settings, then adds a Rule W3 tag issue for each bad artifact tag in instructions.all and instructions.agents.*.

validate_settings runs ostra_sandbox::validate::workspace first, then validate_workspace (ostra-core), then each permission rule through ostra_policy::validate_rule, then checks each absolute project path is a folder. validate_workspace checks the name, project keys, paths, stacks, code providers and language servers, routing agent keys, MCP servers, limits, forbidden routes, and that every route key resolves on every complexity, on an installed harness, with a provider key. The list is sorted by path then message and deduplicated.

With no issues, write_settings calls trust::save_workspace: it stashes file literals, seals MCP secrets, writes workspace.toml through write_file (which drops yolo, limits, the sandbox_* fields, tool_enforcement and permissions.mode), then set_access writes those dropped values to the registry Access record, and records the file hash for command approval when the file was approved. sync_projects then updates the project table.

Later, the runner reaches a spawn step. perform_spawn calls `self.services.workspace()`. ServerServices::workspace re-reads workspace.toml with load_toml_required (falling back to seeded defaults if the file does not parse), applies overlay (registry values over the file), and, if the file is not approved, strips MCP servers, code providers, language servers, allow rules and projects outside the root.

perform_spawn resolves the route from `global` and `settings`, loads project.toml, INVENTORY.md and the project instruction files from disk, and calls `factory.build(&req, &SpawnEnv { state, executor, settings, profile, inventory, repo_root, project_docs })`. A route error or a build Err is recorded as a denied execution, not retried with defaults.

AgentsFactory::build maps SpawnInputs to the agent's typed params, renders the `Label: value` block, then derives from the settings: `projects` (for tag resolution), `instructions_for(agent)` (each passed through with_tagged_files), and the effort via resolve_effort(settings, agent, complexity). It reads ArtifactsBrief and BooksBrief from the workspace folder, not from settings.

augment appends build_brief's output to the first message after a `---` line, unless the message already contains one of the brief headings. build_brief emits, in order: the profile and inventory sections chosen by `sections(agent)`, project instruction files, new projects, artifacts, books (Rule B5, with the Rule B8 search hint), then workspace instructions. It returns None when nothing applies.

patterns.description: The engine never caches workspace settings. perform_spawn calls services.workspace() once per spawn, uses the result for route resolution, and passes a reference to the factory in SpawnEnv. The factory is the only place that decides which settings reach the brief. The brief crate sees no WorkspaceSettings: it receives pre-selected values (instructions: &[String]) in BriefInput.
patterns.name: Settings are re-read through Services::workspace() and passed to the factory in SpawnEnv

patterns.description: ArtifactsBrief::read and BooksBrief::read return None when the folder holds nothing, and build_brief emits a section only for Some. Each section carries a heading constant that augment checks so a message with a brief already in it is returned unchanged. The books block is not tied to any setting today: every agent, including the initializer, receives it when books exist. The block lists at most MAX_BRIEF_BOOKS books and says how to search them from BooksBrief.search_tool, which the factory fills when the agent has Capability::DocsSearch (Rule B8).
patterns.name: Brief inputs are read from disk at spawn time; a section is an Option on BriefInput

patterns.description: Most settings live in .ostra/workspace.toml. The control settings live in the registry under an Access record, are removed from workspace.toml by write_file, and overlay() writes them back over the file's values on every read. A new field that must not be controllable by a folder file needs all of: a field on Access with #[serde(default)], set_access, overlay, write_file's t.remove list, create.rs's adopted-file reset, and (if sandbox) the sandbox() accessor. A field that lives in the file needs none of these. sandbox_blocked_ports is the latest field added this way and shows every touch point.
patterns.name: Two storage locations for workspace settings (Rule A2)

patterns.description: Every validator returns ValidationIssue { path, message } with a dotted or indexed settings path. Layers, in order: ostra_sandbox::validate::workspace (sandbox fields), validate_workspace in ostra-core (name, projects, routing keys and routes, MCP, limits), permission rule parsing and project folder existence in validate_settings, and the Rule W3 instruction tag check in WorkspaceRt::validate. save_settings refuses to write when any issue is returned. Messages follow HANDOVER section 20: the instruction first, then a because clause. A list setting is validated per entry with an indexed path plus a cap constant on the whole list.
patterns.name: Save-time validation: layered validators returning Vec<ValidationIssue>

patterns.description: Model for validating one new setting: a private function per setting in a crate that owns the semantics, called from a public aggregator, with a MAX_ constant and one issue per bad entry plus one for the list as a whole.

patterns.description: SETTING_KEYS lists dotted serialized keys with a one-line description for settings search; the test setting_keys_name_fields fails if a key is not a field of the serialized seeded settings. WorkspaceSettings carries #[serde(default)], so a new field with a Default value loads from an existing workspace.toml without a migration. #[ts(export)] makes cargo test -p ostra-core regenerate web/src/api/gen/WorkspaceSettings.ts.

document.problem: A workspace setting lives in WorkspaceSettings, is stored either in .ostra/workspace.toml or in the registry, is re-read through Services::workspace() on every spawn, and is handed to the spawn factory in SpawnEnv. The factory then selects which settings feed the repo brief; only instructions reach the brief today, and the books section of the brief is built from disk and not from any setting. Save-time validation is a pipeline of three functions plus a tag check, and a rejected value stops the write.

submit.findings_summary: The engine calls Services::workspace() on every spawn. ServerServices re-reads workspace.toml, applies the registry overlay for the control settings (Rule A2), and strips unapproved commands. perform_spawn hands the result to AgentsFactory::build in SpawnEnv. The factory is the only place that selects settings for the brief, and today that is `instructions_for(agent)` and `projects` for tag resolution. The books section comes from BooksBrief::read on disk, not from a setting, and brief.rs never sees WorkspaceSettings. Save goes through PATCH /api/workspaces/{id} to WorkspaceRt::save_settings, which runs validate: ostra_sandbox::validate::workspace, then validate_workspace in ostra-core, then permission rules and project folders, then the Rule W3 tag check. Any issue returns a 422 with {error, issues} and nothing is written. The document records the registry versus file storage touch points and a per-setting validator model with a cap constant and indexed paths.
